title: The Theranos Fraud Explained Like You're 5
hook: She raised seven hundred million dollars for a blood-testing machine that could barely run one test -- and for over a decade, almost nobody outside the building found out.
body:
Elizabeth Holmes dropped out of Stanford at nineteen to build a machine that could run any blood test from a single drop. It couldn't. Most of what Theranos sold to Walgreens, to investors, and to patients ran on modified commercial machines using diluted finger-prick samples -- disclosed only to the FDA, never to the people paying for it. A board of statesmen with no medical background backed her. Two junior employees and a grandson of one of those statesmen tried to say so and were sued and followed for it. A Wall Street Journal reporter got the story anyway. This is what the evidence -- the SEC's complaint, the criminal trial, and the sentencing record -- actually says happened.

For educational and entertainment purposes. Historical events are dramatised; no dialogue in this video is presented as a verbatim quotation except where directly attributed on screen.
pinned: The part that still gets me: the two people who first said something were a lab associate six months into her first job and a board member's own grandson. Not the regulators. What number in this one surprised you most?
